position_in_era.historical_role: The flamenco-guitar virtuoso most often called 'the natural continuation of Paco de Lucía' — a parallel solo-instrument modernizer to Dorantes, exact same generation (Amigo b. 1967, Dorantes b. 1969). *Ciudad de las Ideas* won the 2001 Latin Grammy for Best Flamenco Album; lateral peer to Orobroy on the *guitar* side of the same modernization.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 2000. Won 2001 Latin Grammy for Best Flamenco Album, plus the 2002 Ondas Award for best flamenco work.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Studied for a decade with Manolo Sanlúcar; performed with Paco de Lucía in the *Leyendas de la guitarra* show in Seville.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Córdoba — Amigo's home and the album's titular reference. Album includes 'Córdoba', 'a personal vision of my home, letting everyone know that this place is united with my heart'.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Flamenco guitar lead with full ensemble (cajón, palmas, cante, occasional jazz horn).
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: International flamenco-guitar canon; one of the most-referenced post-Paco solo-guitar albums.
